inconsistencies: Benchmark block fixture overlap: #36254 adds undo data for the existing block413567 fixture while #32554 deletes that fixture entirely in favour of a runtime generator that also produces undo data (and supersedes #32457). Decide the direction first; #36254 is the smaller fix for the misleading verbosity-3 benchmark, #32554 is the broader replacement. #34360 separately extracts fake-block helpers into a shared bench header and should be rebased on whichever lands.

Immutable-primitives chain (#36692): #35994 (clang-tidy automated rewrite) and #36694 (manual declarative rewrite of mempool tests/benches) pursue the same goal; the #35994 author favours the manual route, so #36694 should be reviewed and #35994 treated as superseded.

Unit-test assertion/runner chain: #35713 replaces Boost.Test with an in-tree runner, #35139 adds new thread-safe ASSERT macros, #36091 adds operator<< formatters explicitly to prepare for #35713, and #36074/#36087 touch assertion includes across the same files. Agree on the target framework (#35713) before merging the three macro/formatter PRs, or they will be rewritten twice.
#36437's harness is a stated prerequisite for the follow-up orphanage hole fixes in #36506; reviewing it late stalls that chain.
#35442 bundles and depends on #35433 (RPC deprecation, outside this category); it cannot be merged standalone.

#36455 (dynamic spenders in feature_taproot.py) and #36458 (static script_tests.json / tx_invalid.json vectors) cover the same interpreter edge cases found via bitcoin-s; review #36455 first since the generated asset dump feeds qa-assets, and #36699 also regenerates that dump — these three touch the same asset-generation path and should be ordered.
#36618 strips manual index-sync helpers across 18 functional test files; other test-touching PRs here will conflict textually, so it is worth landing early rather than last.
result.notes: Band distribution after the pass: 2 P1 (framework-wide flake fix and the end-to-end orphanage fuzz harness that found a real bug), 6 P2, 30 P3, 20 P4. Two P3s were raised to P2 only where another P2 on the list does the same kind of work (#36587 alongside #36408 for real test failures, #36082 alongside #35774 for untested release binaries); one P3 was lowered to P4 where reviewers disputed that the coverage it adds is meaningful (#35342). Ordering within P3 follows the category's own priority order: misleading-signal fixes, then high-risk-path coverage (p2p, consensus), then framework capability, then test speed, then benchmarks and downstream vectors, then CI hygiene.
